facts.text: Off-field test methods can be organized by the boundary of the real system under test, progressing outward from software to the electronic control unit (ECU), the sensor and the complete machine.
facts.quote: A useful way to organize the methods is by the boundary of the real system under test.

facts.text: Moving the boundary of the real system under test outward from software to the ECU, sensor and complete machine includes more real failure modes, but increases complexity and reduces test speed, scalability and controllability.
facts.quote: The farther outward that boundary moves, from software, to the electronic control unit (ECU), to the sensor, to the complete machine, the more real failure modes are included, but at the cost of complexity, speed, scalability and controllability.

facts.text: Organizing tests in layers by the boundary of the real system under test matches hardware-in-the-loop and vehicle-in-the-loop practice in the automotive literature.
facts.quote: This layered approach matches hardware-in-the-loop and vehicle-in-the-loop practice in the automotive literature

facts.text: Published vehicle-in-the-loop evidence is predominantly on-road evidence.
facts.quote: the published vehicle-in-the-loop evidence is predominantly on-road.
